description: Replay bounded operations on the pinned Lua table-backed min-heap with a separate signed-i32 priority map.

contract.operation: Replay operations on a fresh table_heap instance whose comparator reads a mutable ID-to-priority map.
contract.comparator: less_than(id_a,id_b) is priority[id_a] < priority[id_b], with strict signed-i32 comparison.
contract.constructor: Build the complete priority map, then heapify initial IDs bottom-up; create the ID-to-index map after heapify.
contract.index_map: Maintain an ID-to-current-heap-index map across every swap, push, pop, replacement, and removal. find_index and ID-based mutations use direct map lookup; linear scans of the heap do not satisfy the source contract.
contract.downheap_ties: Begin with the right child; select the left only when its priority is strictly smaller. Swap only when the chosen child priority is strictly smaller than the parent.
contract.priority_updates: Write a new priority before decrease/increase/replace invokes heapify; retain the old priority through replace/remove comparator decisions.
contract.replace_self: Replacing an ID with itself is a no-op only when its priority is unchanged.
contract.nil_serialization: Lua nil and mutator return values are encoded as INT64_MIN; IDs are signed i32 and cannot collide.
contract.empty_semantics: Empty top and find_index for a missing ID return nil; pop on empty is an invalid trace.

operation_codes.1: top(): all arguments are zero padding
operation_codes.2: pop(): all arguments are zero padding; invalid when empty
operation_codes.3: size(): all arguments are zero padding
operation_codes.4: empty(): all arguments are zero padding

output.encoding: One signed-i64 result per operation in operation order; nil/mutator results are INT64_MIN.
output.error_precedence: Malformed or invalid traces are rejected before output-pointer or capacity checks.

workspace.meaning: At most one signed-i64 result for each of 256 operations.
